solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charge one type of vehicle

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied by the state

explanation.surface: A query about the fee for one kind of vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, one particular kind of road vehicle.

clue.text: Memory loss means I somehow start to ad-lib

indicators.note: somehow says the letters get there in some unspecified way, rearranged
the start of a word is its opening character

explanation.surface: An actor who forgets lines has to improvise.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for loss of memory.

clue.text: Popular place for data loaded to a computer

explanation.surface: A trendy venue for entering data into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the information fed into a computer system for processing.

clue.text: Struggling onward, we gradually overcome resistance

indicators.note: letters that are struggling are writhing about and out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A team plodding forward until the opposition finally gives way.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear down is the idiom for slowly exhausting an opponent's opposition until it gives way.

clue.text: You and I decided — in the end — to get married

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing character

explanation.surface: A couple finally resolving to tie the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to marry, the formal verb for entering a marriage.

clue.text: Drama set around middle of Flemish city

indicators.note: letters moved around are mixed into a new order
the middle of a seven-letter word is its fourth character

explanation.surface: A play staged in a Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flemish city' looks like the definition, but Amsterdam is Dutch; 'Flemish' only supplies its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Sons featuring in proper family tree

indicators.note: something featuring in another appears within it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons

explanation.surface: Male heirs appearing on a respectable genealogy.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent is ancestry or lineage, what a family tree records.

clue.text: Make circular motions with part of foot

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the heel is the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: An exercise instruction to rotate the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn or circle, as birds wheel overhead.

clue.text: Extravagantly fashionable suit

parts.note: spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Praise for a lavishly stylish outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in spades' means in great abundance, to an extreme degree.

clue.text: Stage favourites making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read going back the other way

parts.note: a teacher's pets are their favourites

explanation.surface: Popular performers returning to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process, one phase of a progression.

clue.text: Those heading up promotions should sell things over here!

indicators.note: the words at the head are the starting ones, so only their leading characters are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A sales manager insisting that the promotions team shift stock here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a street seller's furtive call to passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed interjection used to attract someone's attention quietly, like calling 'over here!'

clue.text: In shrewd fashion, clubs and bar finally pool money

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

indicators.note: finally points at the closing character of the word it follows

parts.note: Y stands for yen, Japanese money

explanation.surface: Someone shrewdly gathering cash from golf clubs and a bar into a shared kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverly means astutely or smartly, which is acting in a shrewd way.

clue.text: After cloudiness at first, Fair Isle otherwise clears up

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the first one
at first points to the opening character of the preceding word
otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather report: after early cloud, the sky over Fair Isle brightens.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a remote Scottish island, also a shipping-forecast style place name.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify is to make clear, so something that clarifies clears up a matter or liquid.

clue.text: Strategy mostly pursued by a country in Africa

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final character is dropped
something pursued by another has that other following behind it

parts.note: a gambit is an opening strategy, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A plan mainly carried out by an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African country along the Gambia river.

clue.text: Minor route, I hesitate to say, is more expansive

parts.note: in Britain a B-road is a minor road, below an A-road
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly claiming a back road is wider.
explanation.definitionFit: Broader means wider, so covering a greater expanse.

clue.text: Hate engendered by extremely divisive experiment

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes, the two end letters of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of divisive

explanation.surface: Bitter loathing stirred up by a very controversial trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, a strong synonym of the verb hate.

clue.text: Payment of small gratuity on completion

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A modest tip paid when a job is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, such as a salary or allowance.

clue.text: Nothing found in ghastly premium shop

indicators.note: one thing found in another is sitting inside it
a ghastly version is a horribly mangled one, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Complaining that there is nothing worth buying in an awful upmarket store.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large store or shop, often selling a wide range of goods.

clue.text: Mass requests for protective equipment

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A flood of demands for PPE.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as an adjective, many requests, but it is the abbreviation M.
explanation.definitionFit: Masks cover the face to protect against infection or dust, a kind of protective kit.

clue.text: King boarding large sailing vessel

indicators.note: someone boarding a vessel goes inside it

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch climbing aboard a great sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Publisher's description of obscure book

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A publisher's summary of a little-known book.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the promotional summary printed on a book's cover by its publisher.

clue.text: Senior journalist from America given employment

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: An American editor landing a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in reverse clue order: the American comes first, then the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used has been put to work, i.e. given employment in the sense of being employed.

clue.text: Dignitary occasionally interrupted by discourteous gatecrasher

indicators.note: something interrupted by another has that other breaking into its middle
occasionally means every so often, so only every other character is taken

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of dignitary

explanation.surface: A VIP sometimes interrupted by an ill-mannered party crasher.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters where not invited, just as a gatecrasher turns up uninvited to a party.

clue.text: Couple also outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than seen

explanation.surface: A pair who are both blunt-talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, the number two.

clue.text: Strong drink reporters love after the ends of some shifts

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the first
the two end letters shift places, swapping their order
the ends of a word are its first and last characters

parts.note: first and last letters of some
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Journalists coming off the night shift who love a powerful drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' looks like work shifts, but it tells you to swap the two end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a concentrated coffee, a strong drink in the caffeine sense.

clue.text: People in funks do bounce back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: People who are depressed manage to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: A funk is a low mood; 'bounce back' reads as recovery but only 'back' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bods is British slang for people or persons, as in 'a few odd bods'.
